summary.title: The little book about OS development
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a small x86 operating system from scratch: booting with GRUB, a minimal assembly kernel, moving to C, and the path toward paging, user mode, file systems, system calls and multitasking.
takeaways: How to set up a toolchain (GCC, NASM, ld, genisoimage, Bochs) for building an x86 kernel.
How the boot chain works: BIOS, GRUB loading an ELF kernel via the multiboot magic number.
How to write a minimal assembly kernel, link it at 1 MB with a linker script, and boot it in Bochs.
How to set up a stack in the bss section and call C code from assembly using cdecl, with the flags needed for freestanding C.
summary.summary: This free online book is a practical guide to writing an x86 operating system, produced as a course project at KTH. It covers the tools (GCC, NASM, GNU ld, Bochs, GRUB Legacy), then walks through a minimal kernel that writes 0xCAFEBABE to eax, building an ISO image and running it in the Bochs emulator. Chapter 3 moves to C by setting up a stack, calling C from assembly with cdecl, using packed structs, and compiling with freestanding GCC flags and a Makefile. The table of contents lists later chapters on interrupts, paging, user mode, file systems, system calls and multitasking, which give more outline than step-by-step code.
